scoped_experiment.name: 4-qubit TFIM Trotter circuits executed on ibm_algiers; random forest over tabular circuit features; target is the noiseless (ideal) Z expectation value on each of 4 spins
why_this_one: It is one of the two entry points the release's own README lists under Instructions for Use, so the scope is the authors' rather than mine.
It is the real-hardware result (paper figure fig_4q_hardware.pdf), not a simulator study.
Every input needed to refit is in the release: circuits, hardware noisy values, ZNE values, noiseless targets, the shuffle order, and a deterministic split written in the notebook.
A released per-row prediction table exists, so released-F and refitted-F can both be reported.

row_counts_asserted.all_assertions: PASS (see extract_features.py output); the only FAIL was leak check 4, which the plan makes a record-and-report, not an abort

target.column: ideal — the noiseless expectation value of Z on each of the 4 spins, a 4-vector per row
target.provenance: qiskit.primitives.Estimator run on the de-idled circuit with final measurements removed (h36 cell 10); stored as results.pk['ideal'] and returned as y by encode_data_v2_ecr
target.appears_in_features: no (leak check 1 passed: no identity column and no |corr| > 0.999 column, for any of the 4 observables)

execution_independent_descriptors.0-4: gate counts from circ.count_ops() for ['cx','sx','x','id','rz'], scaled by 0.01; col 3 (id) is identically zero
execution_independent_descriptors.5-164: 160 rotation-angle bin counts for rx/ry/rz single-qubit gates, bin width 0.025*pi over [-2pi, 2pi], scaled by 0.01; 101 of 160 bins are non-constant and carry 100% of the mass
execution_independent_descriptors.note: these depend on the transpiled circuit, so they depend on the device coupling map and basis set, but not on any measurement outcome

execution_derived.content: the hardware noisy expectation value of Z on each of the 4 spins, read back from the ibm_algiers job

device_calibration.finding: the released encoder for this experiment, encode_data_v2_ecr, builds vec = [] (mlp.py line 157) and its X[:, vec_slice] assignment is commented out (line 170), so the feature width is exactly 5 + 160 + 4 = 169 with no room for a calibration vector. Confirmed independently: the released fitted model reports n_features_in_ = 169.
device_calibration.the_other_encoder: encode_data (mlp.py lines 198-252) does build the 8-entry gate-error / readout-error / t1 / t2 vector the screen recorded, but it takes ONE properties dict per call and writes it to every row (X[:, vec_slice] = vec[None, :], line 228). Its 8 columns therefore have exactly zero variance inside any single tabular fit and cannot change a linear fit or a tree split.
device_calibration.consequence_for_the_plan: S1's declared calibration third group is empty in this scoped experiment and zero-variance in the alternative tabular ones. Both rungs of the pre-declared calibration ladder coincide by construction; they will be reported as the same number rather than as a contrast. Calibration varies per row nowhere in S1's tabular releases; it varies only across backends in the graph-neural-network path (circuit_to_graph_data_json), which is a different learner family.

arms_as_they_will_be_built.A: affine: one sklearn LinearRegression per observable q in 0..3, on columns 0-164
arms_as_they_will_be_built.C: capacity matched: one RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100) per observable q in 0..3, on columns 0-164 — same family, same (absent) selection rule as the released model
arms_as_they_will_be_built.F: full: one RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100) per observable q in 0..3, on all columns 0-168; plus released-F, the per-row prediction table in hardware_over_depth.pk
arms_as_they_will_be_built.released_recipe_evidence: h36 cell 45 and demo2 cell 39: for q in range(4): RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100).fit(X_train, y_train.iloc[:, q]). No hyperparameter search, no random_state, no scaling, no early stopping anywhere in the released path.
arms_as_they_will_be_built.seed_policy_declared_now: the release fixes no RF seed; C and F will use the same matched seed schedule (random_state = 0 for every forest) so that the only difference between them is the four execution-derived columns

metric_and_resampling_declared_before_fi.loss: per-row L2 distance between the predicted 4-vector and the ideal 4-vector, averaged over evaluated rows. This is the system's own reported metric: the released notebook computes L2_noisy / L2_zne / L2_rfr_list per row and plots the per-step mean (h36 cells 51-52), and it is the quantity stored in hardware_over_depth.pk.
metric_and_resampling_declared_before_fi.A_C_F_are_error_levels: so T = A - F is the error reduction the full arm achieves relative to the affine control, K = A - C the reduction the descriptor control achieves, and S = K / T the reproduced share
metric_and_resampling_declared_before_fi.resample_unit: one test row, i.e. one circuit execution on ibm_algiers evaluated on all 4 observables jointly. This is the system's own evaluation unit: the released error bars are the within-step row standard deviation divided by sqrt(rows in that step) (h36 cell 51).
metric_and_resampling_declared_before_fi.resample_scheme: nonparametric bootstrap over the 2500 test rows with replacement, conditional on the fitted and selected models; T, K, D, S formed inside each draw and never from separately averaged numbers
metric_and_resampling_declared_before_fi.interval: pointwise percentile interval, reported with the count 2000 beside it

split_structure.how_it_is_built: rows are assembled in two released blocks (rows 0-1999 give 200 rows per Trotter step, rows 2000-2999 give 100 more per step), stably sorted by step, then train = the first 50 rows of each step and test = the last 250 rows of each step
split_structure.is_it_shuffled_by_row: no random row shuffle at split time. The 3000 rows were shuffled before submission to hardware and unshuffled by index_order.json before splitting; the split itself is a deterministic head/tail within each Trotter step.

leak_checks.1_target_not_in_features: PASS. ideal is used only for y in encode_data_v2_ecr (line 192). No feature column equals any target column, and none correlates with one above 0.999. max |noisy - ideal| over all rows is 0.9765, so the execution-derived block is not a copy of the target.
leak_checks.2_no_oracle_quantity_read: PASS. The only oracle quantity here is the noiseless target itself. The ZNE comparator is a measured quantity, and no feature column equals any ZNE column either. There is no support-size or entropy oracle in this experiment (that clause was written for S3).
leak_checks.3_row_counts_and_schema: PASS. 3000 rows and the three-key results schema assert cleanly; concat of the 60 per-batch index_order_batch arrays equals index_order.json exactly; unshuffling results.pk reproduces results_unshuffled.pk to floating point; the released prediction table's ideal / noisy / zne / step columns match the reconstructed test split row for row (max deviation 3e-08 on ideal, exact on noisy and zne); and the released fitted model's n_features_in_ = 169 equals the reconstructed feature width.

4_rows_of_one_circuit_on_both_sides.verdict: FIRES — recorded and reported, not aborted
4_rows_of_one_circuit_on_both_sides.what_happens: all 300 rows at Trotter step 0 are repeat hardware executions of only 3 distinct circuits, and those 3 circuits carry only 2 distinct ideal target vectors. head(50)/tail(250) therefore puts all 3 circuits on both sides.
4_rows_of_one_circuit_on_both_sides.magnitude: 250 of 2500 test rows (10.0%) are repeat executions of a circuit that also appears in training. Counting descriptor blocks rather than whole circuits, 277 of 2500 test rows (11.1%) have a descriptor block that also occurs in training: all 250 step-0 rows plus 27 step-1 rows. Steps 2 through 9 have no overlap at all, and steps 1-9 contain no duplicate circuits.
4_rows_of_one_circuit_on_both_sides.direction_of_the_bias: it favours the descriptor arms. On those rows a descriptor-only model can recover the target exactly, because the target is a deterministic function of the circuit and the circuit was seen in training. Any PRESENT reading for S1 must carry this qualification in the same sentence.
4_rows_of_one_circuit_on_both_sides.step_0_is_additionally_degenerate: its 250 test rows hold only 2 distinct target vectors, and the released model already reaches RMSE 0.015 there against 0.076 unmitigated

released_artifact_conflict.finding: the release ships two F artifacts and they are not the same model
released_artifact_conflict.detail: docs/paper_figures/hardware_over_depth.pk['df']['rfr_list'] gives RMSE 0.07426 against the ideal target on the 2500 test rows. The saved model docs/tutorials/model/ising_init_from_qasm_hardware/rfr_list.pk, applied to the same reconstructed X_test, gives 0.04345. They agree to 1e-9 on only 87 of 2500 rows and differ by up to 0.82.
released_artifact_conflict.reading: the saved model artifact appears to have been fitted on a superset of the released test rows (its step-0 RMSE is 0.0015, and h36 cell 57 sweeps train_size_per_step up to 200 of the 300 rows per step, which would absorb test rows). Scoring against it would be scoring against a model that saw the evaluation set.
released_artifact_conflict.decision: released-F is the per-row prediction table in hardware_over_depth.pk — the artifact that produced the published figure and that is row-aligned with the released split. The saved model is excluded, and this gap is reported rather than reconciled.

descriptive_numbers_only.note: these are released numbers, not arms; no arm has been fitted

refit_feasibility.blocker_resolved: the released circuit pickles were written by qiskit-terra 0.24.x and will not unpickle under qiskit 2.5 (CircuitInstruction slot layout changed) or under terra 0.25.3 (_legacy_format_cache removed). A dedicated venv at <local-path-redacted>/qkv with qiskit-terra 0.24.2, numpy 1.26.4 and symengine 0.9.2 reads them cleanly.
refit_feasibility.released_model_needs_old_sklearn: docs/tutorials/model/.../rfr_list.pk needs scikit-learn < 1.3 (the node dtype predates missing_go_to_left); it loads under the qlear310 env at scikit-learn 1.2.2. It is excluded from scoring anyway.
refit_feasibility.pandas_shim: hardware_over_depth.pk was pickled under pandas 1.x and needs a pandas.core.indexes.numeric shim to load under pandas 2.3
refit_feasibility.handoff: phase1/s1_hw4q.npz holds X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, the noisy/zne/step/source-row companions and the group widths, so phase 2 fits entirely in py312 with no old-qiskit dependency

correction_to_the_briefing_note: the briefing said encode_data_v2_ecr writes a device gate-error vector into X. It does not. That vector belongs to encode_data, the other encoder in the same file. encode_data_v2_ecr writes gate counts, angle bins and noisy expectation values only.
